title: How to add a label in Linear on Mac: steps for the desktop app
metaTitle: How to Add a Label in Linear on Mac: Step by Step
description: Learn how to add a label in Linear on Mac. Open an issue, use the Labels field or press L, then create and manage labels that fit your team.
targetKeyword: how to add a label in linear on mac
intro: To add a label in Linear on Mac, open the issue and click Labels in the right sidebar, or select the issue and press L to open the label picker. Choose the label you want, and if its group allows it, add more.
tldr: Select an issue, press L, type part of the label name, then press Return.
Or open the issue and click the Labels field in the right sidebar.
Groups are single-select by default, so one issue gets one label per group.
Create missing labels in label settings. Label names cannot contain emojis.
Moving an issue to another team removes its team labels.

blocks.text: Labels are small tags you attach to issues in Linear. They help you sort, group and filter work, so a bug report does not get lost next to a feature request. On a Mac, you can add one in a few seconds once you know where the controls are. This page covers the desktop app, the L shortcut, the Labels field, and the rules that decide how many labels one issue can carry.
Desktop app or browser: which one you use

Linear runs in two places. The Linear Desktop app for macOS supports both Intel and Apple silicon Macs, and it updates itself in the background. The web app runs in a browser and supports the three most recent versions of Chrome, Firefox and Safari.

The desktop app adds OS notifications and a Dock unread indicator. Its keyboard shortcuts also clash less with browser shortcuts. That matters for a single key like L, because a browser can grab it first.

The sources I could open do not list a minimum macOS version or an app version number for labels. If your Linear window looks different from the steps here, check for an app update before you assume the steps are wrong.
Add a label with the L shortcut

The fastest route is the L key. Select an issue in the list or on the board, press L, and the label picker opens. Type part of a label name to narrow the list, then press Return on the label you want.
The L shortcut comes from a third-party shortcut sheet, not from Linear's own help pages. Press ? inside Linear to see the shortcut list for your version before you rely on it.

items: Select the issue in the list or on the board.
Press L to open the label picker.
Type part of the name to filter the list.
Press Return on the label you want, then press Esc to close the picker.

blocks.text: Add a label from the Labels field
If you prefer the mouse, open the issue first. In the right sidebar, click the Labels field. The same picker opens, and you can scroll the full list when you are not sure of the exact name.
Use the mouse when you are browsing. Use L when you already know the name and want to move fast through a backlog.

blocks.text: A link such as linear.new?labels=bug,android,comments opens a new issue with those labels already set. Linear's issue docs describe this pre-fill. It runs in a browser, so use it when you want the same setup for several issues or a teammate.
Create a label that does not exist yet

If the label is missing, create it in label settings rather than on the issue. Settings paths differ between sources. Linear's project labels doc says workspace labels live under Settings > Projects > Labels, and team labels live in each team's own settings. Other sources say Settings > Workspace > Labels.
Linear's own labels article did not open when this page was checked. Trust the path you see in your app over any page, including this one.
What to fill in when you create a label
Give the label a short name that a teammate can scan in a list. Pick a color that sets it apart from the others. Then choose the group it belongs to.
Names cannot include emojis. Linear made this change on Sep 3, 2026, so type a plain word or a short phrase instead of a symbol. A name like Bug works. A name with a face or a flag does not.
Single-select and multi-select label groups
Every label belongs to a group. Groups default to single-select, which means an issue can carry only one label from that group. Linear added a multi-select option on Oct 22, 2026.
To change the type, open the label's contextual menu and find Group type. Choose single-select or multi-select. The change decides how many labels from that group one issue can hold.

Here is a worked example. Say you have a group called Area with two labels, Frontend and Backend. While Frontend is on an issue, a single-select group blocks Backend. Remove Frontend, then add Backend.

If the issue really touches both areas, change the group to multi-select. Then both labels can sit on the issue together. Decide this before your team starts tagging, because changing the type later affects every issue that already has labels from the group.

On Nov 5, 2026, Linear changed how label menus show a multi-select group. Each selected label now gets its own row in the menu. In web forms, selected labels show as removable chips, so expect that layout if your team uses multi-select groups.
Filter issues by the labels you add
A label only helps when you can find it later. On Sep 14, 2026, Linear made new label filters default to include any of when every selected label belongs to the same group.

On Sep 3, 2026, Linear added a No labels filter option. Use it to catch issues that still need tagging. For the full filter steps, read [how to filter issues in Linear on Mac](/how-to/filter-issues-in-linear).
What happens when you move an issue to another team
Team labels stay with their team. When you move an issue to another team, Linear removes its team labels. Create the label in the new team first, then move the issue and add the label again.

blocks.title: Check labels before a team move
blocks.text: Moving an issue removes its team labels. Create the same label in the destination team first, then add it back after the move.
Troubleshooting when a label will not add
Most label problems come from one of four causes. Work through them in order, because the first two are the most common.

items: The second label is blocked, because the group is single-select.
The label is missing, because it belongs to another team.
The L key does nothing, because the cursor sits in a text field.
The name is rejected, because it contains an emoji.

blocks.text: If none of those fit, update the desktop app and try again. The app updates itself in the background, but admins can turn that off, so ask an admin if updates never arrive.
Mistakes people make with labels on Mac
The same few mistakes show up in most teams. They are easy to avoid once you see them, and each one costs time later.

items: Creating a near-duplicate label. Type the name in the picker first, and check whether a close match already exists.
Using a single-select group for a value that really needs two answers.
Forgetting that team labels do not follow an issue to another team.
Pressing L while the cursor is in a title box. That types the letter instead of opening the picker.
Adding emojis to label names, which Linear no longer allows.

blocks.text: The fix for most of these is a quick review. Once a month, scan the label list, remove duplicates, and check which groups should allow more than one value.
Next steps after you tag issues

Once labels sit on your issues, you can build views that show only the work you care about. Read [how to switch between list and board in Linear on Mac](/how-to/switch-between-list-and-board-in-linear) to choose the layout that shows labels best.

When you need to work through a batch, [select multiple issues in Linear on Mac](/how-to/select-multiple-issues-in-linear) and review them in one pass. Tagging goes faster when you already know which issues need which labels.
Where Lazur helps with labels on Mac
Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold Option and Command, then ask about what is on your screen. Ask where the Labels field is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

Ask for a walkthrough, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on, so you stay in control of Linear. Lazur does not click for you, and it does not add the label, create the group or change team settings.

Lazur works in any app on screen. The same question works when you switch to a different tool, so you do not need to learn a new help menu for each one. Read [Lazur for Linear on Mac](/apps/linear) to see what it covers, or [download Lazur](/download) to try it on your Mac.
Keep your label list tidy
Labels pile up fast. Every new team member adds one, and soon you have three names for the same thing. A short review keeps the picker useful, so people trust the list and stop inventing new names.
Start with the labels that appear on the most issues. Rename the vague ones, remove the duplicates, and set group types so the rules match how your team works.

faq.question: Can I add more than one label to an issue on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, if the label's group is set to multi-select. Groups default to single-select, which allows one label per group. Linear added the multi-select option on Oct 22, 2026, so check the group type before you assume a limit.

faq.question: What is the shortcut to add a label in Linear on Mac?
faq.answer: Select the issue and press L. That shortcut appears on a third-party shortcut sheet, not in Linear's own docs. Press ? inside Linear to confirm it for your version.

faq.question: Where do I create a new label?
faq.answer: Open label settings, then create the label with a name, a color and a group. The settings path differs between sources, so look for the Labels section in your Settings. If you cannot find it, ask a workspace admin.

faq.question: Why does Linear block my second label?
faq.answer: The label's group is single-select, so only one label from that group can sit on the issue. Remove the label that is already there, then add the new one. Or change the group to multi-select if the issue should carry both.

faq.question: Does a label move with an issue to another team?
faq.answer: No. Moving an issue to another team removes its team labels. Create the label in the new team first, then add it again after the move.

faq.question: Can label names include emojis?
faq.answer: No. Linear stopped allowing emojis in labels on Sep 3, 2026. Use a plain word or a short phrase instead.

faq.question: Is the Mac desktop app different from the web app for labels?
faq.answer: The sources I could open list no separate label steps for each version. The desktop app adds OS notifications and a Dock indicator, and it clashes less with browser shortcuts. Check the picker in your version, and update the app if the menu looks different.

faq.question: Can Lazur add the label for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the Labels field, explains the group rules, or walks you through each click. It does not click buttons or change Linear for you.

steps.name: Open the issue
steps.text: Click the issue in the list or on the board so its detail view opens. You can also select the issue in the list and skip the click, as long as the row stays highlighted.

steps.name: Press L to open the label picker
steps.text: With an issue selected, press L. A label picker opens. The shortcut comes from a third-party sheet, so press ? in Linear to confirm it for your version.
steps.tip: If L types a letter into a title or comment box, click outside the text field first.

steps.name: Or click the Labels field
steps.text: Open the issue and look at the properties in the right sidebar. Click Labels. The same picker opens, and you can type part of a label name to narrow the list.

steps.name: Pick the label
steps.text: Click a label, or highlight it with the arrow keys and press Return. The label appears on the issue. Add more labels if the group allows it.

steps.name: Close the picker
steps.text: Press Esc to close the picker. The label stays on the issue.

steps.name: Create a label if it is missing
steps.text: If the label you want is not in the list, create it in label settings rather than on the issue. Give it a name, pick a color, and choose its group. Names cannot include emojis.
steps.tip: Sources disagree on this path. One Linear doc says Settings > Projects > Labels. Check which one your app shows.

steps.name: Set the group type
steps.text: Open the label's contextual menu and find Group type. Choose single-select, the default, or multi-select. Multi-select lets one issue carry more than one label from the group.

steps.name: Check the team
steps.text: If you work in several teams, make sure the label exists in the team that owns the issue. Team labels do not follow an issue when it moves to another team.

shortcuts.action: Add label to the selected issue

troubleshooting.fix: Click the issue so it is selected, and make sure the cursor is not inside a title or comment box. Press L again. If it still fails, press ? to check the shortcut list for your version.
The label's group is single-select, which allows one label per group. Remove the first label, or change the group type to multi-select from the label's contextual menu.

troubleshooting.problem: The label I need is missing
troubleshooting.fix: The label may belong to another team, and team labels do not show in other teams. Create it in the team that owns the issue, or ask a teammate in that team to check the label settings.
Labels cannot contain emojis, a rule that started on Sep 3, 2026. Rename the label with plain text.

troubleshooting.problem: The label disappeared after a team move
troubleshooting.fix: Moving an issue to another team removes its team labels. Create the label in the new team, then add it again.

troubleshooting.problem: The menu looks different from these steps
troubleshooting.fix: Update the Linear desktop app. It updates itself in the background, but admins can turn that off, so ask your admin if updates never arrive.
